title: Rare, Relevant, and Still Wrong: How Memory Fails LLM Group Decisions
abstract: arXiv:2610.37624v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: When an LLM group's discussion is compressed into a short memory for a final decision maker, what should the memory keep? Two natural heuristics keep the rarest claims or the claims relevant to the decision criteria. On hidden-profile tasks both look attractive, because how widely a fact is held is confounded with whether it helps. We introduce CrossProfile, a diagnostic benchmark of 60 templates with automatically verified answer keys, in which the ownership of supporting, decoy, and irrelevant facts is crossed while their text is held fixed (480 tasks). Across Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, and two DeepSeek models, both heuristics fail in predictable places. Selecting by relevance readmits decoys, because decoys are on topic: even a perfect relevance filter loses 23 to 31 points to rarest-first selection in the classic hidden-profile configuration. translated_title: 稀有、相关却依然出错：记忆如何使大语言模型群体决策失效
translated_abstract: 当一个LLM群体的讨论被压缩成一段简短记忆供最终决策者使用时，这段记忆应该保留什么？两种自然的启发式方法是保留最稀有的论断，或保留与决策标准相关的论断。在隐藏档案任务上，两者看似都很有吸引力，因为一个事实被多少人持有与它是否有帮助是相互混淆的。我们提出了CrossProfile，一个包含60个模板、答案经过自动验证的诊断基准，其中支持性事实、诱饵事实和无关事实的持有分布被交叉设计，而其文本内容保持固定（共480个任务）。在Qwen2.5-7B、Llama-3.1-8B和两个DeepSeek模型上，两种启发式方法都在可预见的地方失败。基于相关性选择会重新引入诱饵信息，因为诱饵是切题的：在经典的隐藏档案配置下，即使是一个完美的相关性过滤器也比最稀有优先选择低23到31分。最稀有优先选择平均而言并不优于随机选择，且仅在……
tldr: 该论文提出CrossProfile诊断基准，通过交叉控制支持性、诱饵和无关事实的持有分布，揭示了LLM群体决策中两种记忆压缩启发式的可预测失败：基于相关性选择会重新引入切题的诱饵信息，而最稀有优先选择平均表现不优于随机选择。
en_tdlr: Introducing CrossProfile, a diagnostic benchmark that crosses the ownership of supporting, decoy, and irrelevant facts while holding text fixed, the paper shows both relevance-based and rarity-based memory selection heuristics fail predictably in LLM group decisions—relevance filtering readmits on-topic decoys while rarest-first selection performs no better than random on average.
